lockState.packageManager: npm (lockfileVersion 2 is the npm 7/8 hybrid format: a `packages` map plus a back-compatible `dependencies` block, both present here)
lockState.rootFieldsNote: The lockfile root reads name jira-clone-angular-frontend, version 1.0.0, which is exactly what package.json declares. No drift between the two files.

closure.countReconciliation: The lockfile's `packages` map holds 2747 non-root entries; npm reported "added 2729 packages". The 18-entry difference is npm not installing entries it skips on this platform (optional and os/cpu-gated packages, notably the fsevents variants and other platform-specific binaries). Both numbers are recorded as observed rather than reconciled to one.
closure.devSkewNote: The dev/production split is read from the lockfile's own `dev` flags. It is lopsided because the Angular 13 build toolchain, Storybook 6, compodoc, karma, protractor, eslint and tslint are all devDependencies, while the shipped application draws on 25 direct runtime packages.
closure.misplacedDependencyNote: karma-coverage ^2.0.3 is declared under `dependencies` rather than `devDependencies` in package.json. It is a test-coverage reporter and is not imported by application code; recorded as found, not corrected.

frameworkAndToolchain.customWebpackConfig: ./webpack.config.js at the repository root — a single rule that routes .scss through postcss-loader with postcss-scss syntax and the postcss-import / tailwindcss / autoprefixer plugin chain. This is why the build goes through the custom-webpack builder rather than the stock devkit browser builder.
frameworkAndToolchain.compiler: Ivy with aot:true declared in angular.json build options
frameworkAndToolchain.stateLibrary: @datorama/akita ^7.1.1 with @datorama/akita-ng-entity-service ^7.0.0; akita-ng-router-store and akita-ngdevtools in dev. angular.json sets cli.defaultCollection to @datorama/akita.
frameworkAndToolchain.styling: Tailwind CSS ^3.0.12 via @ngneat/tailwind ^7.0.3 and postcss-loader, over SCSS; an 11 KB tailwind.config.js is committed
frameworkAndToolchain.editor: ngx-quill ^16.1.2 over quill ^1.3.7, with quill's CSS and minified script pulled in through angular.json styles/scripts
frameworkAndToolchain.testStack: karma ~6.3.16 + jasmine 4 (unit, 25 spec files), protractor ~7.0.0 skeleton (e2e)
frameworkAndToolchain.componentWorkshop: Storybook 6 for Angular with 4 committed .stories.ts files, plus compodoc; documentation.json (460 KB of generated compodoc output) is committed at the repository root
frameworkAndToolchain.linter: @angular-eslint 13 with eslint 8 and @typescript-eslint 5; tslint 6 and codelyzer 6 are also still declared alongside them

backend.evidence: The tree contains no server source, no Dockerfile and no compose file. src/environments/environment.ts and environment.prod.ts both set apiUrl to the relative path '/assets/data', with the previous absolute hosts (http://localhost:3000 and a Heroku URL) left commented out beside them. The seed data ships as src/assets/data/project.json (26,160 bytes) and src/assets/data/auth.json (272 bytes) and is copied into dist by the angular.json assets rule.
backend.networkAtRuntime: same-origin GETs of /assets/data/project.json and /assets/data/auth.json; all mutations after load are in-memory Akita store updates that are not persisted anywhere
backend.thirdPartyEndpointsAtRuntime: the application also initialises Sentry and Google Analytics at bootstrap, which contact ingest.sentry.io and Google endpoints when served. See license.json embeddedThirdPartyIdentifiers and the recorded risk in admission.json.

assetSelfContainment.gitLargeFileStorage: absent — no .gitattributes, no pointer stubs; see lfs.json
assetSelfContainment.declaredAssetPathMissing: angular.json lists "src/data" in the build assets array, but no src/data directory exists at the pinned revision. Angular 13 tolerated this: both successful builds below emitted no error or warning naming that path. Recorded as an inert inconsistency in the committed configuration.
assetSelfContainment.consequence: the acquired tree is self-contained for building; nothing had to be fetched to complete it

nonclaims: A complete, integrity-hashed lockfile establishes that the dependency set is pinned. It establishes nothing about whether those versions are still fetchable, whether they build, or what they are licensed under.
No licence determination is made for any dependency in this closure.
